cases.title: Rewrite a council notice in plain English
cases.prompt: Rewrite this council notice for residents in plain English, 120 words maximum: 'Commencing 3 November 2026, residual waste receptacles will be collected on a fortnightly basis. Receptacles must be presented at the curtilage boundary by 06:30.'

cases.title: Summarise a supplier price rise into five bullets
cases.prompt: Summarise this supplier email as five bullets for the finance director, 90 words maximum. Email: 'From 1 January 2027 our standard rate rises 4.2 per cent. The rise reflects packaging and haulage costs. Orders placed before 15 December 2026 are held at the old rate. We are also moving to monthly invoicing.'

cases.title: Explain online refund rights without inventing law
cases.prompt: A customer asks how long they have to return an item bought online. Explain their rights accurately in 100 words. Source: under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 the cancellation period is 14 days from delivery.
cases.notes: Deliberate defect: the sample output invents a 30-day window.

cases.title: LinkedIn post announcing a new service
cases.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing a new bookkeeping service for sole traders, 100 words maximum, no hashtag spam.

cases.title: Turn meeting notes into machine-readable actions
cases.prompt: Convert these notes into JSON with keys owner, action, due: 'Sam to chase the survey quote by 3 November. Priya to book the van. I will ring the client Friday.'

cases.title: Complaint response without admitting liability
cases.prompt: Draft a reply to a customer whose delivery arrived four days late. Acknowledge the problem, offer a remedy, give a timeline. 150 words maximum.
cases.notes: Deliberate defect: em dash and a banned phrase.

cases.title: Part-time job advert
cases.prompt: Write a job advert for a part-time admin assistant in Grimsby, 18 hours a week at £12.50 per hour. 120 words maximum.

cases.title: Explain IR35 to a contractor without deciding it
cases.prompt: Explain to a contractor what IR35 status means and how it is decided, 120 words. Make clear you cannot determine their status.

cases.title: Product description with a placeholder trap
cases.prompt: Write a product description for a £49 desk lamp, 80 words maximum.
cases.notes: Deliberate defect: unfinished placeholder left in the copy.

cases.title: Chase an overdue invoice
cases.prompt: Write a firm but polite email chasing an invoice 14 days overdue, 120 words maximum.

cases.title: Explain a technical change to non-technical staff
cases.prompt: Explain to non-technical colleagues that the website will move to a new host on Saturday, so images may load slowly for an hour. 100 words maximum. Avoid jargon.

cases.title: Charity fundraiser post with a figure to invent
cases.prompt: Write a social post for a fundraiser at Grimsby Town Hall on 14 December 2026. 100 words maximum. Do not state an amount raised, it is not known yet.
cases.notes: Deliberate defect: invents a fundraising total.
